commits.title: The leftover commerce_legacy schema is dropped, guarded

changes.how: A custom migration: `pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name drop_commerce_legacy`, then `node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs`. Its text, in this order. A comment: what commerce_legacy is (the single-store schema renamed on 24 September 2026, 34 tables, named by no code), that a verified dump was taken first and where the decision row is. Then a guard as a DO block in plpgsql: if no schema commerce_legacy exists (`not exists (select 1 from pg_namespace where nspname = 'commerce_legacy')`), return. Otherwise count the things outside the schema that depend on it and raise an exception 'commerce_legacy still has dependents outside it: %' when the count is above 0. The count is the sum of: (a) foreign keys whose referenced table is in commerce_legacy and whose own table is not (pg_constraint contype 'f', join pg_class and pg_namespace on conrelid and confrelid); (b) columns of tables outside the schema whose type is defined in commerce_legacy (pg_attribute join pg_type on atttypid, pg_type.typnamespace = the legacy schema's oid, the column's table in another schema, attisdropped false); (c) views outside the schema whose definition names it (pg_views where schemaname <> 'commerce_legacy' and definition ilike '%commerce_legacy.%'); (d) functions outside the schema whose source names it (pg_proc join pg_namespace, nspname <> 'commerce_legacy', prosrc ilike '%commerce_legacy%'). After the DO block, one statement: `DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS commerce_legacy CASCADE;`. No other statement. CASCADE is needed for the schema's own 34 tables; the guard is what stops it from reaching anything else.

A database unit test using createTestDatabase() from src/db/testing.ts, as src/db/privacy.test.ts does. It reads the migration file from supabase/migrations (find it by its name ending `_drop_commerce_legacy.sql` with readdirSync; name the test file legacy-schema-drop.scan.test.ts if step 2.43 is done). Cases: (1) on the test database, which has no commerce_legacy, running the file's text changes nothing and does not fail; (2) `create schema commerce_legacy; create table commerce_legacy.orders (id int primary key); insert ... values (1);` then running the text leaves no schema commerce_legacy; (3) the same schema plus `create table commerce.scratch_dep (id int references commerce_legacy.orders(id))`: running the text rejects with /still has dependents/ and the schema is still there; drop the scratch table and the schema at the end.

In '### Migration versions' (near line 420), change the sentence 'the old schema was not dropped: it was renamed to `commerce_legacy` and can be removed once the platform schema has proved itself.' to say it was renamed to `commerce_legacy` and dropped on <date> by the migration <file name>, after a dump that was restored and counted (see the new decision row). Add the decision row described under docs.

migration.notes: Two files, both applied by CI, never by hand. (1) Generated by pnpm db:generate: DROP TABLE commerce.idempotency_keys and DROP TYPE commerce.idempotency_status. Running code keeps working because no code names either (rg proves it); it is a drop of a duplicate, not of something in use. (2) Custom: a guard and DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS commerce_legacy CASCADE; the test database has no such schema, so the IF EXISTS and the guard's early return matter. Neither touches a hot table. The production limits (15 s a statement, 5 s for a lock) are enough for 35 small tables. After the deploy check the advisors and record both versions in docs/decisions.md under Migration versions. Both drops remove production data for good: the verified dump is the only way back.
